title: Dilations on the Coordinate Plane
seo_title: Grade 8 Dilations Worksheets: Scale Factor and the Coordinate Plane (TEKS 8.3C, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.3A generalize that the ratio of corresponding sides of similar shapes are proportional, including a shape and its dilation; 8.3B compare and contrast the attributes of a shape and its dilation(s) on a coordinate plane; 8.3C use an algebraic representation to explain the effect of a given positive rational scale factor applied to two-dimensional figures on a coordinate plane with the origin as the center of dilation; 8.10D model the effect on linear and area measurements of dilated two-dimensional shapes
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 dilation worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.3 and 8.10D: dilate points from the origin, scale factors, the rule (kx, ky), proportional sides and the effect on perimeter and area. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Dilation from the origin: (x, y) → (kx, ky).
key_sub: Perimeter × k, area × k². Angles stay the same.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A dilation centered at the origin multiplies both coordinates by the scale factor k: (x, y) → (kx, ky).
  • k > 1 is an enlargement; 0 < k < 1 is a reduction.
  • Angles and orientation stay the same; side lengths are multiplied by k. The image is similar to the original.
  • Perimeter is multiplied by k; area is multiplied by k².

Examples

Example

Dilate (4, −2) by k = 1/2

(1/2 × 4, 1/2 × −2)

Answer: (2, −1)

Example

Area 9 cm², k = 3

9 × 3²

Answer: 81 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the scale factor(x, y) → (kx, ky), not (x + k, y + k).
Thinking a dilation keeps the sizeOnly k = 1 keeps the size.
Multiplying the area by kArea grows by k².

faq.a: Use an algebraic representation to explain the effect of a given positive rational scale factor applied to two-dimensional figures on a coordinate plane with the origin as the center of dilation.
Model the effect on linear and area measurements of dilated two-dimensional shapes.

faq.q: Is a dilation a rigid transformation?
faq.a: No. It changes size, so it does not keep congruence unless k = 1.
Generalize that the ratio of corresponding sides of similar shapes are proportional, including a shape and its dilation.

items.q: Dilate (2, 3) by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What is the image?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × 2, 3 × 2). The image is (4, 6).

items.q: A dilation has scale factor 3. A side is 4 cm long. How long is the side in the image?
items.e: Multiply by 3: 4 × 3 = 12 cm.

items.q: Dilate (4, −1) by a scale factor of 3 with center at the origin. What is the image?
c: (1 13, −13)
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 3: (4 × 3, −1 × 3). The image is (12, −3).

items.q: A dilation has scale factor 1/2. What happens to the figure?
items.e: A scale factor between 0 and 1 shrinks it: it gets smaller.

items.q: Dilate (6, 8) by a scale factor of 12 with center at the origin. What is the image?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 12: (6 × 12, 8 × 12). The image is (3, 4).

items.q: Which move can change the size of a figure?
items.e: Only a dilation changes the size.

items.q: Dilate (−3, 5) by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What is the image?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (−3 × 2, 5 × 2). The image is (−6, 10).

items.q: A(2, 5) is dilated to A′(6, 15). What is the scale factor?
Dilate (9, −6) by a scale factor of 13 with center at the origin. What is the image?
c: (9 13, −5 23)
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 13: (9 × 13, −6 × 13). The image is (3, −2).

items.q: After a dilation, which stays the same?
items.e: A dilation keeps the shape, so the angle measures stay the same.

items.q: Dilate (1, 4) by a scale factor of 4 with center at the origin. What is the image?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 4: (1 × 4, 4 × 4). The image is (4, 16).

Dilate (−2, −2) by a scale factor of 3 with center at the origin. What is the image?
c: (−23, −23)
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 3: (−2 × 3, −2 × 3). The image is (−6, −6).

items.q: A square with side 5 is dilated by 2. What is the new perimeter?
items.e: New side = 10, perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40.

items.q: Dilate (10, 0) by a scale factor of 15 with center at the origin. What is the image?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 15: (10 × 15, 0 × 15). The image is (2, 0).

items.q: Which rule is a dilation with scale factor 4 from the origin?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 4: (x, y) → (4x, 4y).

items.q: Dilate (−4, 6) by a scale factor of 1 12 with center at the origin. What is the image?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 1 12: (−4 × 1 12, 6 × 1 12). The image is (−6, 9).

items.q: A dilation with scale factor 1 does what?
c: Nothing: the figure stays the same
items.e: Multiplying by 1 changes nothing: the figure stays the same.

items.q: Dilate (5, −2) by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What is the image?

items.e: 16 ÷ 4 = 4. The scale factor is 4, so it is an enlargement.

sets.title: The dilation rule and enlargement or reduction

items.q: A figure is dilated by (x, y) → (32x, 32y). Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: The scale factor 32 is greater than 1, so it is an enlargement.

items.q: Which rule describes a dilation with scale factor 12 centered at the origin?
c: (x, y) → (x ÷ 12, y ÷ 12)
(x, y) → (x + 12, y + 12)
(x, y) → (12x, 12y)
items.e: A dilation from the origin multiplies both coordinates by the scale factor: (12x, 12y).

items.q: A figure is dilated by (x, y) → (14x, 14y). Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: The scale factor 14 is less than 1, so it is a reduction.

items.q: Which rule describes a dilation with scale factor 14 centered at the origin?
c: (x, y) → (x + 14, y + 14)
(x, y) → (14x, 14y)
(x, y) → (x ÷ 14, y ÷ 14)
items.e: A dilation from the origin multiplies both coordinates by the scale factor: (14x, 14y).

items.q: A figure is dilated by (x, y) → (3x, 3y). Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: The scale factor 3 is greater than 1, so it is an enlargement.

items.q: Which rule describes a dilation with scale factor 3 centered at the origin?
items.e: A dilation from the origin multiplies both coordinates by the scale factor: (3x, 3y).

items.q: A figure is dilated by (x, y) → (2x, 2y). Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: The scale factor 2 is greater than 1, so it is an enlargement.

items.q: A figure is dilated by (x, y) → (12x, 12y). Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: The scale factor 12 is less than 1, so it is a reduction.

items.q: A figure is dilated by (x, y) → (4x, 4y). Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: The scale factor 4 is greater than 1, so it is an enlargement.

items.q: Which rule describes a dilation with scale factor 2 centered at the origin?
items.e: A dilation from the origin multiplies both coordinates by the scale factor: (2x, 2y).

items.q: Which ratio is the same for every pair of matching sides in a figure and its dilation?
items.e: Matching sides are proportional: image ÷ original = scale factor.

items.q: A triangle is dilated by a scale factor of 3. What happens to its angle measures?
items.e: Dilations keep the shape: angle measures stay the same.

items.q: Which attribute changes when a figure is dilated by a scale factor of 1/2?
items.e: Every side length is halved; angles and orientation stay the same.

items.q: A rectangle is dilated by a scale factor of 1. What is true?
c: The image is half as big
The image is twice as big
The image is congruent to the original
items.e: A scale factor of 1 keeps every length: the image is congruent.

items.q: A dilation has a scale factor between 0 and 1. What kind of dilation is it?
items.e: Scale factors less than 1 make the figure smaller.

items.q: A figure is dilated by a scale factor of 2. Which statement is true?
c: The image is similar to the original but not congruent
The image is congruent to the original
items.e: The sides change length, so the image is similar, not congruent.

items.q: Which moves always give a congruent figure?
items.e: These rigid motions keep size and shape: translations, reflections and rotations.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: It is a reflection over the y-axis, so the size and shape stay the same. Congruent.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: Every side is twice as long (a dilation by 2): same shape, different size. Similar but not congruent.

items.q: Two figures are similar. Which must be true?
c: They are in the same place
items.e: Similar figures have the same shape: their angles are equal and their sides are in proportion.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 3, 4 and 5. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 3. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 5?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Multiply: 5 × 2 = 10.

items.q: Rectangle A is 4 cm wide and 6 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 10 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 10 ÷ 4 = 52. Height = 6 × 52 = 15 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 6, 8 and 10. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 3 that matches the side of 6. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 8?
items.e: Scale factor = 3 ÷ 6 = 12. Multiply: 8 × 12 = 4.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 cm wide and 5 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 12 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Height = 5 × 4 = 20 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 12 and 13. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 36 that matches the side of 12. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 5?
items.e: Scale factor = 36 ÷ 12 = 3. Multiply: 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: Two similar triangles have scale factor 3. The small one has perimeter 12 cm. What is the perimeter of the large one?
items.e: Perimeter scales by the same factor: 12 × 3 = 36 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 4, 6 and 7. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 4. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 7?

Triangle 1 has sides 7, 7 and 10. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 14 that matches the side of 7. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 10?
items.e: Scale factor = 14 ÷ 7 = 2. Multiply: 10 × 2 = 20.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 10, 15 and 20. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 15. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 10?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 15 = 25. Multiply: 10 × 25 = 4.

items.q: A model car is 1/24 of the real size. The model is 18 cm long. How long is the real car?
Triangle 1 has sides 6, 9 and 12. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 8 that matches the side of 6. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 12?
items.e: Scale factor = 8 ÷ 6 = 43. Multiply: 12 × 43 = 16.

items.q: Leo says a 2 × 3 rectangle and a 4 × 5 rectangle are similar because he added 2 to each side. Is he right?
c: No, you must multiply, not add
items.e: 4/2 = 2 but 5/3 ≠ 2: no, you must multiply, not add.

items.q: A figure has an area of 45 square centimeters. It is dilated by a scale factor of 2. What is the new area?
items.e: Area is multiplied by the scale factor squared: 45 × (2)² = 180 square centimeters.
